item.title: Gerontechnology and Inclusive Digital Systems: Affordances, Trust, and AI in Aging Societies
item.content:encoded:
Min Ho Ryu, Dong-A University

One-Ki Daniel Lee, Virginia Commonwealth University

Hanbyul Choi, Dong-A University

Yongbok Cho, Dong-A University

As populations age, older adults increasingly rely on digital systems for care, finance, public services and social connection. While these systems can enhance independence and access, they also create barriers when poorly designed or when they compromise security and autonomy. This special issue examines how digital system design, implementation and governance affect older adults' ability to participate safely and independently in later life.

The special issue brings together research on gerontechnology, information systems, behavioral science and public policy. It seeks empirical, conceptual and design-oriented studies that examine how older adults interact with technology, how trust and safety are maintained, how AI can support autonomy while remaining accountable, and how organizations can make digital services more inclusive across diverse cultural and geographic contexts.

Appel publié par Information Technology & People. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

Potential topics

  • Digital technology use by older adults and proxy use
  • Accessibility and inclusive design in healthcare and financial systems
  • Trust, safety and security in digital systems for older adults
  • AI-enabled services and human-AI interaction in aging
  • Organizational implementation and interoperability of digital services
